item.title: Optimising nonlinear calibration of glass pH electrodes over the pH range −4.5 to 15.5 using improved statistical treatment of acid and alkaline errors
item.authors: Saleesongsom S, Plancherel Y, Weiss D
item.summary: Glass pH electrodes lose accuracy in strongly acidic and alkaline solutions. This study compares seven nonlinear calibration models and identifies an asymmetric double-logistic function that describes electrode behaviour from pH −4.5 to 15.5 at 25 °C. Compared with conventional three-point calibration, it reduces extreme-pH bias by up to 3.0 units in acidic solutions and 1.5 units in alkaline solutions. Statistical tests identify a smaller set of calibration standards that maintains accuracy within ±0.25 pH unit at the extremes while cutting calibration time by at least half.
